Finite-gap approximation and a convergent all-words generating series give lower/upper entropy bounds even for nonsofic infinite S. Strict entropy loss comes from deleting a positive transition. Locally uniform convergence of the tail derivatives and the mean-value theorem yield the exact 1/mu leading product. The standalone checker passed 288 finite validations and is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The motivating article isolates two-ended zero holes as a gap in its general perturbation analysis. The result resolves a natural nonsofic subfamily with one central 1 and no restrictions on the infinite allowed-gap set, showing the entropy drop depends multiplicatively on two separately computable gap tails. The asymptotic has no ratio constraint on the two hole depths, and hence captures both balanced and strongly asymmetric regimes. This is a structural entropy law, not merely a numerical example or finite-table computation.
